Patient is a 54-year-old male presenting with a three-week history of intermittent chest discomfort radiating to the left shoulder, worse on exertion and relieved by rest. Past medical history notable for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. Current medications include lisinopril and atorvastatin. Vitals within normal limits; cardiovascular exam unremarkable. EKG shows normal sinus rhythm with no acute ischemic changes. Plan: stress test scheduled for next week, continue current medications, return to clinic for results.
